title: Arrays and objects
summary: Read and update arrays and objects without surprising mutations.

scenario.briefing: Two widgets share the same student object and overwrite each other's changes. Write a function that returns a new object with an updated field.

objectives.description: Return a new object with an updated field.
Work with array length and indices.

hints: Spread the original object into a new one.

misconceptions.description: Mutating the input object instead of copying.
misconceptions.testDescription: Does not mutate the original object.
misconceptions.feedback: Mutating shared state causes bugs. Return a new object.

misconceptions.description: Believing two object literals are equal by value.
misconceptions.feedback: Objects are compared by reference, not deep value.

sections.title: Arrays
sections.body: Arrays are ordered, zero-indexed collections. Use length, indices, and methods like push and map. Arrays are objects, so mutating one reference affects all aliases.

sections.title: Objects
sections.body: Objects store key-value pairs. Destructuring and spread create shallow copies. Mutating a shared object affects every reference to it.
